result.summary:
REVIEWER gate on REQ-186 -- PASS. Independently read lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260829020001_create_timers.exs, the application.ex/tenant_provisioning.ex diffs, both design docs, docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-186 entry, and lib/letflow/dlq.ex for comparison. Full findings in handoffs/WF02-REQ186-20260829/reviewer-report-req186.md.

Idiom (Q1): PASS. Letflow.Scheduler is a plain Ecto context module matching Letflow.Dlq's shape (opts :: [prefix: ...] threaded through every call, tenant_id server-derived, never caller-supplied). fetch_and_lock_timer/2's FOR UPDATE idiom mirrors Dlq's fetch_and_lock_entry/3. Letflow.Scheduler.Timer mirrors Dlq.Entry's multi-changeset-per-write-path shape exactly. Letflow.Scheduler.Poller is a real supervised GenServer ticker, config read fresh every tick, not a case-based hand-rolled state machine standing in for gen_statem -- this table is CRUD-lifecycle, no gen_statem indicated.

Supervision (Q2): PASS. Poller is one new, ordinarily-supervised GenServer child of Letflow.Application's tree. No new Task.Supervisor added -- verified by grep across application.ex/scheduler.ex/poller.ex, consistent with REQ-185's own explicit decision and REVIEWER sign-off record. config/test.exs's start_scheduler: false gate is a narrowly-scoped, well-justified deviation (documented DBConnection.OwnershipError failure mode under Sandbox :manual mode), same shape as the existing http_child/0 start_http gate -- not unauthorized scope creep.

Scope creep (Q3): PASS. git diff main...HEAD --stat touches exactly REQ-186's design §0 file list plus test-support accounting updates (table/event-type counts) and handoff bookkeeping. No route/controller file, no lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex change (REQ-187's territory, confirmed absent), no lib/letflow/dlq.ex modification (only Dlq.enqueue/2 is called, per REQ-185 §8), no mix.exs change (no Oban). rearm_changeset/2 is defined-but-unused, explicitly flagged in both design and schema moduledoc as reserved for REQ-188 -- a named atom only, no smuggled-in logic or schema surface; not scope creep.

Decision-record consistency (Q4): PASS. Decision 0003 Decision B (schema-per-tenant, tenant_id retained intra-schema) matches. All seven of REQ-185's decisions checked individually against the shipped code -- supervised GenServer ticker, no Oban, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim, no startup-sweep lock, per-tenant-schema iteration, per-timer transaction-only isolation (no new process boundary), exhausted timer to dlq_entries entry_type "timer" -- none silently re-decided. Config defaults (5000/0/64/3) match exactly, read fresh via Application.get_env/3, no compile-time caching.

Design-vs-implementation fidelity: PASS. Schema columns/types, both CHECK constraints (verbatim SQL), partial index, changeset-per-write-path shape, poll-and-fire never-raises contract, two-transaction failure-accounting structure, TIMER_FIRED payload shape, and DLQ enqueue_attrs() field mapping all match the design doc line for line.

actor_id deviation: RESOLVED via a design-doc correction, made directly (REQ-168/REQ-181 precedent). Verified against lib/letflow/event_store.ex (fetch_uuid/3 at lines 221-222/337 rejects nil actor_id; platform_actor_id/0 at lines 771/791 is the established sentinel) that the design doc's literal actor_id: nil is non-functional -- following it would make every fire_timer/2 call fail with :missing_actor_id and never fire a timer. Edited lib/letflow/design/req186-scheduler-core.md section 6 to state the corrected actor_id: EventStore.platform_actor_id() value with full reasoning, marked explicitly as a post-implementation correction. Committed alongside this review.

Verdict: PASS. Routing to TEST-DESIGNER.
